introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Statistics Paper 2 (0770/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : tous les corrigés sont rédigés et chaque valeur numérique a été recalculée par script (sympy).

Le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question ni pour l'épreuve ; les points imprimés par bloc ((i), (ii)...) sont recopiés tels quels (leur somme est 103). Quand un même total couvre plusieurs sous-questions (ex. « (9 marks) » pour (a) et (b)), il est porté par la dernière sous-question du bloc, les autres ont `points` null, et `points` de chaque exercice est laissé vide.

Scan de 3 pages (page de garde + 2 pages de questions) : les questions 1 à 10 sont complètes et se suivent, aucune page ne semble manquer. L'étiquette en haut à gauche de la page de garde dit « Pure Maths With Stats 2 », en accord avec le cadre (Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 2, code 0770) et le pied de page 00/0770/2.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the sum-to-product formulae $\sin A + \sin B = 2\sin\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2}$ and $\cos A + \cos B = 2\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2}$ with $A = 3\theta$, $B = \theta$, so $\dfrac{A + B}{2} = 2\theta$ and $\dfrac{A - B}{2} = \theta$:
$$\sin 3\theta + \sin\theta = 2\sin 2\theta\cos\theta, \qquad \cos 3\theta + \cos\theta = 2\cos 2\theta\cos\theta.$$
Therefore, for all $\theta$ for which the fraction is defined ($\cos\theta \ne 0$ and $\cos 2\theta \ne 0$),
$$\frac{\sin 3\theta + \sin\theta}{\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta} = \frac{2\sin 2\theta\cos\theta}{2\cos 2\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{\sin 2\theta}{\cos 2\theta} = \tan 2\theta. \qquad \blacksquare$$
(Numerical check at $\theta = 20^\circ$: $\dfrac{\sin 60^\circ + \sin 20^\circ}{\cos 60^\circ + \cos 20^\circ} = \dfrac{1.2080}{1.4397} = 0.8391 = \tan 40^\circ$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \cos x + \sqrt3\sin x$, express $f(x)$ in the form $R\cos(x - \lambda)$, where $R > 0$ and $0 < \lambda < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand: $R\cos(x - \lambda) = R\cos\lambda\cos x + R\sin\lambda\sin x$. Equate the coefficients of $\cos x$ and $\sin x$ with those of $f(x)$:
$$R\cos\lambda = 1, \qquad R\sin\lambda = \sqrt3.$$
Squaring and adding: $R^2 = 1 + 3 = 4$, so $R = 2$ (as $R > 0$). Dividing: $\tan\lambda = \sqrt3$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ ($60^\circ$); this is acute, and $\cos\lambda = \tfrac12 > 0$, $\sin\lambda = \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2} > 0$ agree with the signs of $R\cos\lambda = 1$ and $R\sin\lambda = \sqrt3$.
$$\boxed{f(x) = 2\cos\!\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence find the minimum value of $\dfrac{1}{1 + |f(x)|}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $-1 \le \cos\!\left(x - \frac\pi3\right) \le 1$, we have $-2 \le f(x) \le 2$, so $0 \le |f(x)| \le 2$ and
$$1 \le 1 + |f(x)| \le 3.$$
The denominator is positive, so the fraction $\dfrac{1}{1 + |f(x)|}$ is smallest when the denominator is largest, i.e. when $|f(x)| = 2$:
$$\text{minimum} = \frac{1}{1 + 2} = \frac13.$$
This occurs when $\cos\!\left(x - \frac\pi3\right) = \pm1$, i.e. $x = \dfrac\pi3 + k\pi$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. (The maximum value is $1$, when $f(x) = 0$.)
$$\boxed{\text{Minimum value} = \dfrac13}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence find the general solution of $f(x) = \sqrt3$. (8 marks for part (ii), (a), (b) and (c) together)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using $f(x) = 2\cos\!\left(x - \frac\pi3\right)$:
$$2\cos\!\left(x - \frac\pi3\right) = \sqrt3 \;\Rightarrow\; \cos\!\left(x - \frac\pi3\right) = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$
The principal value is $\dfrac\pi6$ (since $\cos\frac\pi6 = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}$). The general solution of $\cos\alpha = \cos\beta$ is $\alpha = 2k\pi \pm \beta$, so
$$x - \frac\pi3 = 2k\pi \pm \frac\pi6, \qquad k \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
- With the plus sign: $x = \dfrac\pi3 + \dfrac\pi6 + 2k\pi = \dfrac\pi2 + 2k\pi$.
- With the minus sign: $x = \dfrac\pi3 - \dfrac\pi6 + 2k\pi = \dfrac\pi6 + 2k\pi$.

Check: $x = \frac\pi2$: $\cos\frac\pi2 + \sqrt3\sin\frac\pi2 = \sqrt3$; $x = \frac\pi6$: $\frac{\sqrt3}{2} + \sqrt3\cdot\frac12 = \sqrt3$.
$$\boxed{x = \frac\pi6 + 2k\pi \ \text{ or } \ x = \frac\pi2 + 2k\pi, \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}}$$
(in degrees: $x = 30^\circ + 360^\circ k$ or $x = 90^\circ + 360^\circ k$).
